title: Kulak's Woodshed
venue_description:
About Kulak's Woodshed

Kulak's Woodshed is a remarkable 49-seat professional recording studio and live music venue that has been serving the Los Angeles singer-songwriter community since 1999. Created by Paul Kulak as a labor of love - this non-profit venue is operated entirely by skilled volunteers and supported by audience donations.

Recording Excellence

What sets Kulak's apart is its commitment to documenting every performance with professional-grade quality. The venue features 5 HD cameras and 24-track Pro Tools audio recording equipment - ensuring that every performer leaves with high-quality video and audio recordings of their set. All events are broadcast live on the internet - and the venue maintains an extensive archive of performances that showcases the incredible talent that has graced its stage.

The Space

The interior is a visual feast of vintage Americana - with dark green painted walls adorned with record albums - collectors' books - toys and bric-a-brac from bygone eras. A baby grand piano serves as the centerpiece of the room - surrounded by guitars - stand-up basses and a full drum kit. The atmosphere evokes 90s living room vibes - creating an intimate and comfortable environment for both performers and audiences.

Community and Accessibility

Kulak's Woodshed welcomes all ages and music styles in a supportive - non-judgmental environment. The venue is alcohol and drug-free - making it accessible to performers and audience members of all ages. Self-serve snacks - soft drinks - tea and coffee are available. The space is even pet-friendly - reflecting the inclusive community spirit that defines the venue.

Weekly Events

Monday nights feature the beloved open mic - where approximately 25 performers are selected via lottery between 7:00-7:30 PM. The venue also hosts ticketed performances throughout the week - featuring both emerging artists and established professionals. Past performers have included Grammy winners and up-and-coming talent who appreciate the venue's artist-friendly approach and professional recording capabilities.

Location and Legacy

Located in the NoHo Arts District on Laurel Canyon Boulevard - Kulak's Woodshed has become one of the Valley's best-kept secrets and was voted the Best Open Mic in the Los Angeles area. The venue continues to serve as a vital incubator for musical talent - providing a supportive platform for artists to develop their craft - connect with fellow musicians and share their art with an appreciative audience.
location: 5230 1/2 Laurel Canyon Blvd - North Hollywood - CA 91607

title: The World Stage Performance Gallery
venue_description:
About The World Stage

The World Stage Performance Gallery stands as one of Los Angeles' most important cultural institutions - founded in 1989 by the legendary jazz drummer Billy Higgins and poet and community arts activist Kamau Daáood. Located in Leimert Park Village - the heart of Los Angeles' African American cultural community - this 100-capacity venue has grown from a loose collective of artists into a pioneering force in South LA's music and arts landscape.

Mission and Vision

The World Stage's mission is to secure - preserve and advance the position of African American music - literature and works in the oral tradition to local - national and international audiences. The venue fills a crucial cultural void by providing a space where jazz occupies an important position within the fabric of the community - fostering an ongoing jazz-driven cultural revolution.

Educational Programming

Through its comprehensive weekly workshop schedule - The World Stage provides quality arts education that links youth with elders in the African American cultural tradition. Monday features the Drum Workshop for children of all ages - continuing the legacy started by Billy Higgins. Tuesday offers Jazz Vocal Workshop. Wednesday hosts the Anansi Writer's Workshop for literary arts. Thursday presents both the Women's African Drum Circle and the Billy Higgins Instrumental Jam Session. Saturday includes the Trap Drum Workshop for children and the Jazz Workshop. Sunday rounds out the week with the Woodwind Workshop and the Rose Gales Vocal Jam Session.

Workshop Philosophy

Workshops are generally offered to the public for suggested donations of $5 to $15 - but importantly - no one is turned away for lack of funds. These sessions operate as informal jam sessions where participants gain intimate understanding of rhythm - percussion - vocal techniques and instrumental performance. The environment fosters exchange and interaction between artists of all ages and levels - providing a place for self-discovery - experimentation and critical feedback in a nourishing setting.

Performance Events

Beyond workshops - The World Stage hosts ticketed performances typically on Friday and Saturday evenings. These concerts feature both local talent and nationally acclaimed artists - including special events like the Kwanzaa Music Festival and the monthly Leimert Park Jazz Festival Sunday Jazz Concert Series. Recent performances have featured renowned musicians and emerging voices in the jazz community.

Alumni and Impact

The fruits of The World Stage's nurturing environment are evident in its many notable alumni who have honed their creative skills through training and exposure at the venue. Alumni include musical groups like B Sharp Jazz Quartet - Young World Stage All-Stars and Black Note; bestselling authors Michael Datcher and Jenoyne Adams; Pulitzer Prize nominee Ruth Forman; acclaimed vocalist Dwight Trible; Sundance Film Fellow Nyesha Khalfani; and author - poet - publisher and radio personality Peter J. Harris.

Sacred Space

The World Stage has evolved into what many consider a sacred space in the Los Angeles music community. It represents more than just a performance venue - it's a place where cultural heritage is preserved - artistic excellence is cultivated and community bonds are strengthened through the transformative power of music and the arts. The venue continues to honor Billy Higgins' legacy while adapting to serve new generations of artists and audiences.

title: Sam First
venue_description:
About Sam First

Sam First is Los Angeles' premier jazz club for world-class modern - eclectic and straight-ahead jazz - uniquely positioned just minutes from Los Angeles International Airport. Operating as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization - Sam First is dedicated to supporting and expanding jazz as a musical form and tradition while providing a vibrant center for regional - national and international jazz practitioners.

The Vision

Owner Paul Solomon created Sam First to be unexpectedly creative - a space that would excite visitors and match the authentic creativity of the musicians who perform there. The venue is named after Sam First - an old-world tailor who led his family to Los Angeles - whose brilliant smile warmed his grandson's heart and inspired the creation of this special space.

Unique Design

Sam First's design philosophy centers on removing barriers between performers and audiences. The venue features no elevated stage - instead creating an intimate configuration where patrons feel like they're on stage with the band. The industrial interior structures are complemented by original photography (shot by Solomon himself) and authentic vintage mid-century modern furniture from legendary designers like Herman Miller and Artemide. The carefully curated aesthetic creates an environment that inspires both musicians and patrons.

Exceptional Acoustics

The listening room features amazing acoustics and is home to one of LA's most loved Yamaha C7x grand pianos. The combination of superior room acoustics and world-class instrumentation creates an irresistible listening experience. Sam First is committed to creating an immersive environment - requesting that guests refrain from talking during performances out of respect for the artists and fellow audience members.

Performance Schedule

Sam First presents two sets nightly - Tuesday through Saturday - at 7:30 PM and 9:30 PM. The venue is closed Sunday and Monday. Tuesday nights feature a special program called The Happenings - where trumpeter Julien Knowles leads an incredible group for one set - followed by an open jam session from 9:00-11:00 PM (jam participants use code SAM1JAM). The venue also hosts College Night - a program designed to give young musicians valuable performance experience and networking opportunities with the wider Sam First family of artists and audiences.

Sam First Records

The venue is also home to Sam First Records - a label that documents performances by resident and visiting artists. Recent releases have featured Grammy-nominated ensembles and acclaimed musicians - capturing the exceptional quality of performances that take place in this intimate space.

Hospitality

Sam First offers a carefully curated selection of craft cocktails - local beers and wines - and bar snacks that pair perfectly with an evening of jazz. The venue provides eight reserved parking spots in the rear of the building (first come - first served after 6:00 PM) - plus nearby metered parking and airport parking lots with special rates for Sam First patrons.

Community Impact

As a nonprofit organization - Sam First fosters growth and engagement of the jazz community in Los Angeles. The venue promotes in-person collaboration - formation of new relationships and creation of original music that takes risks and pushes boundaries. By featuring today's best modern and straight-ahead jazz artists in such an intimate setting - Sam First continues to advance jazz as a living - evolving art form while honoring its rich traditions.
location: 6171 W Century Blvd #180 - Los Angeles - CA 90045

title: The Mint LA
venue_description:
About The Mint LA

The Mint stands as one of Los Angeles' most enduring music venues - having served the city's live music scene continuously since 1937. Located at 6010 West Pico Boulevard just east of Crescent Heights - this intimate club has survived nearly 90 years while many other LA venues have come and gone - earning its place as a true Los Angeles landmark.

Historic Legacy

The Mint's early endeavors in music date back to the 1950s - and the venue quickly became known for hosting legendary artists across multiple genres. An astounding roster of musical icons have either played or broke at The Mint - including Stevie Wonder - Willie Dixon - Natalie Cole - Ray Charles - Leo Nocentelli (The Meters) - Herbie Hancock - Lou Rawls - and many others. This tradition continues with more recent performances by Ben Harper - Macy Gray - Billy Bob Thornton - The Wallflowers - Bonnie Raitt - Jackson Browne - and surprise visits from stars like Johnny Depp and George Clinton.

Venue Characteristics

Despite its low ceilings - The Mint offers unmatched prestige and an exceptional listening experience. The venue was acoustically engineered as a recording studio - providing patrons with profoundly excellent sound quality. The intimate room features excellent sight lines - ensuring every seat offers a great view of the stage. The space maintains the down-home - funky atmosphere that has made it a beloved gathering place for generations of music lovers.

Evolution and Expansion

When musician Jed Ojeda started renting the club for blues band gigs in the mid-1980s - The Mint was a mere 1,000 square feet - a long shotgun-style room with a bar along one wall and a narrow ledge on the other. In 1990 - Ojeda acquired the club and has since overseen its growth while maintaining its intimate character. The venue has expanded to include full restaurant and bar service - while preserving the comfortable - welcoming vibe that defines The Mint experience.

Music Programming

While The Mint has hosted everything from blues and soul to folk and rock over the decades - it remains a prime location for discovering new talent across genres. Jazz Sunday has become a cherished 20-year tradition - featuring rotating selections of LA's best jazz musicians and culminating in the Kevin Kanner Jazz Jam that welcomes participating musicians after 9:00 PM.

Current Operations

The Mint operates as a full-scale restaurant and bar - serving food and drinks throughout all shows. The venue offers various rental options including private events - film shoots - commercial lockouts and green room rentals. Band booking inquiries are welcomed - though the venue receives many requests due to its prestigious reputation.

Practical Advantages

One of The Mint's greatest assets is its location - offering the rare combination of being just 5 minutes south of Hollywood and 10-15 minutes from the Westside - with the added bonus of ample free street parking and minimal traffic. Valet parking is also available most nights. This convenience - combined with the venue's rich history and excellent acoustics - has helped The Mint remain a cornerstone of LA's live music scene for nearly nine decades.
location: 6010 W Pico Blvd - Los Angeles - CA 90035

title: Oracle Tavern
venue_description:
About Oracle Tavern

Oracle Tavern is a welcoming neighborhood bar located at 1640 N Spring Street - just outside of Chinatown in downtown Los Angeles. The venue has become an important gathering spot for the Southern California bluegrass community - hosting a monthly jam session on the second Thursday of each month.

Bluegrass Programming

The monthly bluegrass jam at Oracle Tavern brings together musicians and enthusiasts from across the Los Angeles area. Sessions begin at 8:00 PM and follow traditional bluegrass jam etiquette - with musicians sitting in a circle and taking turns leading songs. The format welcomes players of all skill levels playing acoustic instruments including banjo - fiddle - guitar - mandolin - dobro and upright bass.

Atmosphere and Community

Oracle Tavern provides a casual - friendly environment that has made it a valued part of LA's bluegrass scene. The venue offers full bar service and comfortable seating - creating an inviting space for musicians to connect - share tunes and keep the tradition of bluegrass music alive in Los Angeles. The monthly gatherings have helped build a community of pickers who appreciate having a regular downtown location to play traditional bluegrass - old-time and country classics.

Location

Situated in the historic Chinatown area - Oracle Tavern is easily accessible from various parts of Los Angeles and has become a reliable destination for bluegrass enthusiasts looking for regular jam opportunities in the city.
location: 1640 N Spring St - Los Angeles - CA 90012

title: George Izay Park
venue_description:
About Burbank Bluegrass Jam at George Izay Park

George Izay Park in Burbank has become home to a vibrant weekly bluegrass jam session that takes place every Sunday afternoon from noon to 3:00 PM. Located at the intersection of W Clark Avenue and N Griffith Park Drive - this free outdoor gathering brings together bluegrass musicians and enthusiasts under the shade of beautiful sycamore trees.

Jam Origins and Growth

Started in May 2024 by guitarist and supply chain manager Mark Gusick - the Burbank Bluegrass Jam was created to provide a regular gathering place for acoustic music lovers in the San Fernando Valley. The positive response has been overwhelming - with the group continuing to grow and evolve each week. What began as a small gathering has developed into a thriving community event that welcomes musicians of all ages and skill levels.

Format and Repertoire

The jam follows typical bluegrass etiquette - with musicians arranged in a circle format where each person takes turns leading and singing. The setlist includes a rich mix of old-time - bluegrass and country classics such as Will the Circle Be Unbroken - Old Joe Clark - Arkansas Traveler - Cluck Old Hen and Wildwood Flower. The emphasis is on traditional American roots music played on acoustic instruments.

Instruments and Participants

Regular participants bring and play a variety of instruments including banjos - fiddles - double bass - piano accordion - Dobro resonator guitars and acoustic guitars. The jam has attracted a diverse group of musicians - from 12-year-old fiddle prodigies to visiting musicians from Scotland to seasoned local players. Some attendees even bring wooden dance boards for flatfoot dancing - adding to the authentic old-time atmosphere.

Community Spirit

The gathering embodies the people's music ethos that defines bluegrass and old-time traditions. As organizer Mark Gusick notes - this music creates a real shared bond between fans and players alike - truly representing music by the people for the people. The welcoming - inclusive atmosphere makes it an ideal place for both experienced musicians to jam and newcomers to learn by participating.

Connection to Wider Music Scene

Organizer Mark Gusick and his wife Margo lead the Americana acoustic band Wild Rust - whose version of Wildwood Flower by the Carter Family has been featured over 50 times on KXLU 88.9 FM as the theme for The Wildwood Flower Radio Hour. The couple is scheduled for multiple in-studio performances at the station - demonstrating the connection between this grassroots jam and the broader Los Angeles acoustic music community.

Accessibility

The jam is completely free and open to all - requiring no sign-ups or reservations. Musicians simply need to bring their acoustic instruments and a love of traditional music. The outdoor park setting provides ample space - fresh air and a relaxed environment perfect for making music together. The location in Burbank makes it accessible to musicians from throughout the San Fernando Valley and greater Los Angeles area.
location: W Clark Ave & N Griffith Park Dr - Burbank - CA 91506
